name: Igor Spasojevic
title: Assistant Professor
fitReason: Recent Assistant Professor with strong learning-based trajectory generation and learned semantic perception integrated into real robot navigation. The strongest hardware belongs to prior Penn collaborations; a current UCR visitor invitation or local equipment commitment has not been established.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full CoRL 2025 sequence-modeling paper, including its proceedings PDF, trains an LSTM encoder-decoder on simulated trajectories and executes the resulting references on a real CrazyFlie 2.0 with Vicon tracking. Section 5.2 uses eight paths and repeated learned/baseline trials; classical geometric feedback follows the learned trajectory. Appendix C.3 reports crashes for one alternate model/path, so this is not universal safety. Separately, SlideSLAM 2024–2025 uses YOLO/RangeNet learned detection with geometric factor-graph SLAM. Its Experiment 2 has actual autonomous Falcon 250/Scarab exploration and online semantic map use. Outdoor/forest runs include manual piloting and playback; those are not autonomous field-control trials. Both are Penn-era collaborative evidence, not verified current UCR hardware.

shortVisit.summary: The current official profile confirms a faculty role and public email but contains no visitor or intern invitation. The 2025 UCR research seminar establishes current learning-augmented robotics direction; a seminar open to students is not recruitment. No outside-master summer 2027, duration, remote or funding offer was verified.
